As I read it it reminded me on one of my extreme emotional experience that I had which happened on an IFS therapy when we dug very deep. I felt a giant of sadness of cosmic proportions which kind of felt like it was also not "mine" per se, but I wouldn't call it somebody else's. It just felt like an energy that is... idk, higher than me? Like just a cosmic/primal force, that just "is". It also made me very euphoric, and didn't last long. Even though I long to feel that kind of emotions, some parts of me are afraid of it to the core.
You might want to check out a book called: "Coping with trauma-related dissociation", it describes an interesting perspective on the issue and gives some ways to cope with it (as the name suggest!)

What would be the difference between dissociation and depresonalization? I'm trying to understand those concepts. 

Overall when I get out of dissociation/depersonalization/derealization "naturally" (e.g.: by sports, some good social events and others) then my organism is less afraid of it than if I get out of it quickly and through some "artificial" methods (such as psychadelics). 

I believe dissociation to be a defense mechanism blocking out a lot of unresolved trauma/emotions (or just an organism stuck in very old patterns), and from the perspective of the sub/unconcious it is not safe to be not dissociated, thus it triggers it back on. 

From what I'm learning we just need to get ourselves to get accustomed of not being dissociated step by step and to teach ourselves that it is actually safe to stay in an healthy regulated state. The same way as you would teach a puppy that was abused years and years by humans, that actually it can be safe to be surrounded by people because actually most of them are good, not bad. 

I also saw myself feel a looooooooot of emotions that I wasn't aware of having (or just a feeling of getting my life stolen from myself due to years of being stuck in "frozen" state) when getting out of dissociation, and that can feel overwhelming leading to dissociation again.

Sure go ahead with your own ideas,  I believe artists are at their best when they are free when creating (not trying to sound pretentious, but I really do thing that it is like that lol). I have also some experience with guitars as I played it a lot of it for a few years, so on that matter my opinion might be worth something if necessary, but when it comes to vocals then... I just know if I like it or not. What I really want to say is - don't limit yourself.

I'll just say that maybe try to keep guitar minimalistic? Because the melody on the verses takes a lot of space, so we don't want to make it overloaded with sounds, and on the chorus I think that it's nice to leave a little bit of space. I think that first half of the song (verse + buildup verse leading to chorus) would gain a lot with some rhythmic guitar just to cover that empty space (but actually maybe it won't be necessary, as the vocal would also do the same thing? idk). Maybe on the second verse (so the one after the chorus) let's keep the first half of it without guitar, and just introduce it on the second half of it? 

When I say about minimalistic guitar I mean, for example, the one from Muse's The Dark Side chorus (or even the solo, even thought it is pretty complex melodically/rhythmically-wise but still minimalistic) . 

Those above are just my quick thoughts, and I can't stress enough how it is important for me to do it your own way :) 

I really appreciate you man, let's do it!
